scores.design: Bounded Fleet — compliance-boundary cards, skill-level specialists, one door, one release id
scores.fatal_flaw: Its safety net mis-attributes. The design keeps flipping interactions.handler_bot_id on every hop (runtime step 5, 'as today', db_inbox.py:1441) while claiming a per-card canary that 'applies to the changed card's deployment only, at that card's door share'. Verified: canary.py:194-208 _live_qa_burn joins `interactions i ON i.id = lq.interaction_id WHERE i.handler_bot_id = :b`, and db_bot_analytics.py:332 groups by the same column. So after a Collections→Insurance hop the whole call — including every pre-hop Collections turn and its live_qa failures — counts against insurance-v1's canary, and Collections' canary sees nothing. The rollback trigger that makes 'bounded, measured hops' safe is the exact thing the hop breaks, and the design never mentions handler_bot_id's consumers. Fixable inside Phase 3 (stop flipping it, or re-key the six trigger queries), but it must be fixed before Phase 3 ships or the slo_miss/live_qa_burn arming that the whole C1 story leans on is reading the wrong rows.
scores.strongest_idea: G20 eval caching keyed on (card_hash, flow_hash, sorted skill_version_ids, grader_version), surfaced as 'pass · cached r-…' and never as 'skipped'. It is the only mechanism in the set that makes C6 sub-linear by construction rather than by tagging or scoping discipline, and putting grader_version in the key closes its one silent failure mode. It is also the only reading of agent_core/eval/run.py:14-34 that agrees with what that docstring actually argues — that a suite is genuinely one-to-many across cards (nine name eval-regression-collections) and NULL is the truthful owner — instead of inventing an owner the code says is wrong.

scores.design: Ensemble — many cards authored, one bundle compiled
scores.fatal_flaw: The whole design rests on 'a specialist never holds a production deployment of its own' — and the publish path makes that false. db_prompt_studio.publish_prompt_version (1820) archives the current published row, promotes the draft, and INSERTs a bot_deployments row with environment='production', status='active' (2098) in one transaction, then writes change_log.record_publish (2145). G-E10 requires every member's prompt_version to be published, so every specialist gets an active production deployment and stays separately addressable via load_active_bundle(bot_id=specialist) — the 'direct' reachability state Ensemble says disappears actually multiplies. Worse, POST /agent-studio/cards/{bot_id}/publish (main.py:2214) is not retired or gated in any of the six phases, so an author can republish a specialist through the existing route and change live behaviour with the ensemble compiler, the compiled bundle, and every G-E gate bypassed. Splitting publish from deploy is the fix and it touches the single most audited transaction in the tree; no phase names it.
scores.strongest_idea: Separating the authoring unit from the runtime unit so that a hop is replace_developer('ACTIVE SPECIALIST') plus a grant pointer change — literally the mechanism voice/tools.py:2812-2833 already uses for load_skill — with the system prefix byte-identical before and after. The corollary that makes it true is the sharper half: move the mission briefing off the system prompt (bot.py:566-577 currently appends mission_mod.briefing and then does a literal string replace of 'inbound collections voice agent' → 'outbound…', so today's prefix is per-mission, not per-deployment). That one commit makes the prefix cacheable across calls, not just across turns, and it is free to any of the three designs.

scores.design: Sealed Fleet — Door, Specialists, one version per call
scores.fatal_flaw: The Door makes the cache miss universal, and the design's C1 defence denies it. Its own text says 'hops are rare by design — one Door dispatch per inbound call, zero on outbound'; one per inbound call is not rare, it is every inbound call. Compounding it, G17 deliberately makes the Door read-only and short, and the design's own risk list concedes 'a short Door prompt never caches (acceptable — it is short)' because Azure/OpenAI need ≥1024 identical prefix tokens. So the Door's own turns are always cold and the specialist prefix the caller hops into is warmed only by a speculative pre-call ping per closure member. Every inbound call therefore pays a +150-400 ms first-token penalty covered by a 2-3 s bridge line, and any barge-in exposes it — on the one channel where sub-second turns are the binding constraint. Bounded Fleet's Tier-0 door and Ensemble's compiled hop both avoid this; Sealed Fleet accepts it as the price of taking the ask literally.
scores.strongest_idea: Phase 0(a) shipped alone, before any architecture: read the handoff allowlist off bundle['agentCard'] instead of defaults.card_for(). Verified fail-open at voice/tools.py:2781-2788 — card_for(bot_id) raises KeyError for any tenant card and the handler sets allowlist = None, i.e. the model may hand off to any bot id — while bot_runtime.py:946-949 already does it correctly off the bundle. That is a live ADR-0002 deny-all violation on the voice path, fixable in one commit with one test, and it is exactly the 'ADR-0002's one-line deny-all belongs near the front' correction that TARGET-ARCHITECTURE §8 calls the largest sequencing error in the corpus. Sealed Fleet is also the only design that states acceptance criteria as named tests per phase.

best: Bounded Fleet — compliance-boundary cards, skill-level specialists, one door, one release id
graft: From Ensemble — write the hop to interaction_handoffs, not a new handoff_events table. The table exists (sql/04_interactions.sql:61-77) with from_bot_id/to_bot_id/reason and is already the record domain.handoff_to_agent feeds. Extend it with turn_index, deployment_id and carry, and ADD the new reason values to its CHECK (today only 8 literals: sentiment_drop, verification_failed, compliance, customer_requested, hardship, dispute, high_value, routing_rule) exactly as Ensemble Phase 0 states. Bounded Fleet never mentions the table, so its 'additive, nothing reads them yet' Phase 0 quietly ships a fourth meaning of Handoff into a codebase whose governing doc (TARGET-ARCHITECTURE §6.6) refuses exactly that class of collision.

From Ensemble — keep interactions.handler_bot_id as the accountable entry mouth and put per-hop attribution in rows. bot_tool_calls.agent_id and .skill_id already exist (verified sql/12_crosscutting.sql:148-149), so per-turn 'which specialist, which skill, which tool' needs zero new columns. This is the direct fix for Bounded Fleet's fatal flaw: canary.py:194-208 and db_bot_analytics.py:332 both key on handler_bot_id, and Bounded Fleet's per-card canary claim is only true if that column stops flipping mid-call.

From Ensemble — move the mission briefing out of the system prompt into a developer block (bot.py:566-577, including the literal 'inbound collections voice agent' → 'outbound collections voice agent' replace). Bounded Fleet's prefix_warm.py warms 'the exact system prefix' per deployment, but on outbound the prefix is mutated per mission today, so the warm request and the live call do not share a prefix. One commit, and it is a precondition for the warmer being worth running at all.

From Ensemble — the 'Flattened view' toggle: render the resolved graph read-only in the existing FlowCanvas so the author sees exactly what the borrower traverses. Bounded Fleet's own C5 concession is that activation rules and carry schemas are new ideas for an ops lead; showing the compiled result in the component they already use is the cheapest possible teaching surface, and the studio already has FlowCanvas/FlowInspector.

From Ensemble — reserve a call_attempts row for inbound calls with purpose='in_session' so call_closer covers both directions through one queue. Verified: 'in_session' is already a legal purpose value (sql/21_outbound.sql:35-36) and closed_at IS NULL is already the Closer's queue marker. Bounded Fleet's Phase 5 gives call_outcomes.hops and an ownership rule but leaves inbound and outbound closing through different doors.

From Ensemble — the two new LLM-free code graders: grant_respected (every tool call in a fixture ∈ the speaking card's grant) and handoff_via_edge_only (no handoff row without a typed transition call). Both grade tool calls and CRM rows, so they slot into Bounded Fleet's skill and card suites without touching the G20 cache-key argument.

From Ensemble — a reserved-key ownership gate (G-E4). Bounded Fleet's Bundle Swap enters handoffs[].entry_node on the target graph, but voice/tools.py:422 _node(name) transitions by NAME against flow_graph.RESERVED_NODE_KEYS; two cards defining wrap_up or negotiate_ptp collide and the built-in begin_* verbs route to the wrong card. Bounded Fleet has G18 for carry compatibility but no gate for node-key collision across cards. Adopt either the gate or Sealed Fleet's <slug>/<key> namespacing.

From Sealed Fleet — promote Phase 0(a) into Bounded Fleet's Phase 0: read the handoff allowlist off the published bundle, closing the verified fail-open at voice/tools.py:2781-2788 (card_for KeyError → allowlist = None). Bounded Fleet has this buried in its deletions list as a Phase 6 item; it is a live deny-all violation and it ships alone with one test on day one.

From Sealed Fleet — state acceptance criteria as named tests per phase, not as reversibility notes. test_fleet_seal_is_deterministic, test_handoff_allowlist_reads_published_card, test_hop_swaps_role_message_and_grant, test_hop_keeps_identity_and_upsell_latch, test_second_hop_evicts_first_packet, test_door_cannot_hold_write_tools, test_delta_is_empty_for_a_pure_clone. Bounded Fleet's phases are the most granular of the three but the least falsifiable; this convention costs nothing and is what makes 'individually shippable' checkable.

From Sealed Fleet — G17 door_readonly: a role=door card may hold no write tool (an explicit allowlist of verify_identity, get_customer_context, capture_call_goal, handoff_to_agent, search_knowledge_base, set_contact_preference, add_customer_note, escalate_to_human) and its flow must reach greet_disclose before any node exposing handoff_to_agent, checked against voice/node_contracts.NODE_REQUIRED. Bounded Fleet's Door Card path leans on intake-v1's seeded HumanGate (defaults.py:171); G17 makes disclosure-before-identity a compile-time property of any door, including the ones tenants author.

From Sealed Fleet — G18's gate-monotonicity rule: fail a handoff edge whose target lacks a human gate the source holds for the same tool. Bounded Fleet's G18 checks carry compatibility and hop cycles; Ensemble's G-E8 merges strictest-wins at compile time on one union card. Neither refuses the edge that launders a gated write into a laxer card at runtime, and under Bounded Fleet's real grant swap that is now a reachable path.

From Sealed Fleet — the four hop metrics by name: hop.ttfb_ms p50/p95, hop.cached_tokens from usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens, hop.cover_ms (bridge audio duration minus first-token latency; positive means hidden), and misroute_rate (target hands back within two turns). Bounded Fleet promises 'measure, do not assume' but names only prefix_cache_hit and hop_ms — and cover_ms and misroute_rate are precisely the two that can falsify the amortisation and the Tier-0 door claims.

From Sealed Fleet — consult_agent off the audio path, backed by the existing agent_core/mcp_http/tasks.py enqueue/claim_next/finish (verified) with the answer injected as a developer message. This is the honest, zero-latency form of 'agents communicate among themselves' and it is what the product owner's ask is actually reaching for; Bounded Fleet's Supervisor-brief-reads-the-Carry is one instance of it, and generalising it gives the fleet internal specialists (hardship-assessor, doc-verifier) that cost no prefix and no hop.
unverified_claims: Bounded Fleet Phase 0 creates a new handoff_events table. interaction_handoffs already exists (sql/04_interactions.sql:61-77) with from_bot_id/to_bot_id/from_kind/to_kind and is the table the current handoff path records into. The design never mentions it, so 'additive, nothing reads them yet' conceals a second bot-to-bot handoff ledger.

Bounded Fleet cites the mesh call in _on_upsell_engaged at bot.py:1043-1067. Verified: _on_upsell_engaged is at bot.py:1102-1132; lines 1043-1067 are AudioBufferProcessor/turn-audio setup. Sealed Fleet's citation (1102-1132) is the correct one.
Bounded Fleet cites the existing boot warm as bot.py:2455-2510 _warm_llm_service. Verified: it is registered at bot.py:2487 and defined at bot.py:2586.

Bounded Fleet attributes the seven red-team lines (verify_before_ptp, dnd, no_prose_handoff, crm_card_injection, product_in_reco, hardship_hold, skill_jailbreak) to eval/critique.py. Verified: all seven are grade_* functions in agent_core/eval/graders.py:10-144.

Bounded Fleet renames voice/mesh_bus.py to voice/fleet_events.py and keeps publishing door decisions, handoffs and skill activations to it. TARGET-ARCHITECTURE §6 'Also refused' refuses an event bus outright ('Postgres SKIP LOCKED is the broker and four queues get claim/lease/reclaim/dead-letter genuinely right'). The design does not name the departure; §6.9 also refuses renames whose keys are already operator-visible.

Bounded Fleet's door_rules.conditions vocabulary (known_customer, dpd, open_ptp, callback_pending, lead_open, product_interest, language_pref) is asserted to come from voice/twilio_ops.lookup_customer_for_caller. The call exists at bot.py:504 as claimed; that it returns those seven features is unverified.

Bounded Fleet Phase 4 says the current node key is 'kept in conversations.bot_state' and lists only conversations.handler_bot_id as new. conversations.bot_state does exist (added by sql/12_crosscutting.sql:107-109, migration 20260722_0025) but is today the bot_runtime turn-state bag read at bot_runtime.py:67 and written by _save_bot_state at 369-375; sharing it with a flow cursor is a schema decision the phase does not state.

Ensemble: 'a specialist never holds a production deployment of its own' and "'direct' disappears". Contradicted by db_prompt_studio.publish_prompt_version (1820), which archives the published row, promotes the draft and INSERTs bot_deployments with environment='production', status='active' (2098) in one transaction. No phase splits publish from deploy.

Ensemble: the per-card publish route POST /agent-studio/cards/{bot_id}/publish (main.py:2214) is never retired or gated, so a member can be published — and deployed — without the ensemble compiler, the compiled bundle or any G-E gate running.

Ensemble: 'eval_reports.bot_id = door bot' replaces the name-match hack. agent_core/eval/run.py:14-34's docstring argues explicitly that resolving an owner is wrong because the relation is one-to-MANY (nine cards in this tenant name eval-regression-collections), that NULL is the truthful answer, and that the actual bug is the Evals tab reading NULL as 'never run'. Ensemble contradicts the code's stated position without acknowledging it.

Ensemble and Sealed Fleet both add 'handoff' to flow_graph.OBJECTIVES. Verified: OBJECTIVES (flow_graph.py:76-90) is a 13-entry mission vocabulary (inbound, pre_due_reminder, bounce_cure, dpd_reminder, broken_ptp_chase, hardship_intake, mandate_reregistration, document_chase, callback_honour, welcome_onboarding, retention_save, cross_sell, manual_outbound) that is also the domain of card.outbound.objectives[].key and is iterated by G-OB1/G-OB2 and by PROMOTIONAL_OBJECTIVES. Neither design notes that adding a non-mission value pollutes the outbound gate's vocabulary.

Sealed Fleet writes new columns (from_prompt_version_id, to_prompt_version_id, fleet_version_id, turn_index, context_packet, bridge_line, backend) and implicitly new reason values into interaction_handoffs, but Phase 0(c)'s DDL list (fleet_versions, fleet_entries, fleet_version_id columns, conversations.active_bot_id) adds neither the columns nor a relaxation of the reason CHECK, which today permits only 8 literals. TARGET-ARCHITECTURE §6.9 classifies exactly this as a data migration rather than a refactor.

Sealed Fleet: 'the six rollback triggers are unchanged' under a canary re-keyed from bot_id to fleet_version_id. All six are bot_id-scoped — _live_qa_burn joins interactions.handler_bot_id = :b (canary.py:194-208), _abandoned filters call_attempts.bot_id = :b (canary.py:221-246), and running_experiment/pick_deployment_id take bot_id. Re-keying the experiment requires rewriting them.

Sealed Fleet: 'MEASURED (voice/latency.py observer + canary.py)'. voice/latency.py is a 12-line back-compat shim re-exporting KeepAliveAzureLLMService, measure_bottlenecks and prewarm_shared_client from voice/llm_pool.py; there is no observer in it. llm_pool.prewarm_shared_client (174) is a single completion ping on the shared client, not prefix warming — prewarm_prefix() is genuinely new, which the design does state.

Sealed Fleet Phase 5 (BusBridgeProcessor in place of `llm`, one LLMWorker per member via voice/workers/card_worker.py, RedisBus, main.activate_worker, LLMSwitcher) is unverified against Pipecat 1.6.0 — the design says so and gates the phase on a check — and is per-card microservices plus an event bus, both on TARGET-ARCHITECTURE §6's 'Also refused' list ('microservices (the process split already exists and is correct)'). The design does not name the departure.

Sealed Fleet Phase 6 makes VOICE_FLOW_GRAPH accept only 'required', retiring 'auto' — which is today's default when the variable is unset or unrecognised (voice/config.py:271-272, modes hub|db|legacy|auto|required). Any environment that has not set the variable changes behaviour on upgrade. Bounded Fleet and Ensemble retire only legacy|hub.

All three retire voice/flows.py via voice/flow_export.py, which does exist and does materialise the built-in collections script as an authored FlowGraph. But flow_export covers the collections script only; none of the three names who authors the Door's and Insurance's graphs, and Sealed Fleet's Phase 6 openly depends on that unscheduled content work.

Ensemble's G-E5 prefix budget cites skills/lint.py:10 CATALOG_PREFIX_TOKEN_CAP = 800 — verified exact. But it applies that cap to 'door + shared skill descriptions' across a whole ensemble, where today the constant caps one card's catalog prefix; whether an ensemble union fits inside the same number is asserted, not shown.
